items.title: Xaluritamig Trial in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial is testing the safety of xaluritamig, a new drug, in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC). The study is currently recruiting patients to determine if the drug is safe and to find the right dose. This is an early-stage trial exploring a new treatment option for advanced prostate cancer that no longer responds to hormone therapy.

items.title: Xaluritamig Combined With Hormone Therapy for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial tests xaluritamig combined with standard hormone treatments (darolutamide or abiraterone) in patients with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and aims to determine if this combination is safe and tolerable. This represents a potential new approach to treating cancer that has spread but still responds to hormones.

items.title: Different Dosing Schedules for Lu-177 PSMA in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares different dosing schedules of Lu-177 PSMA (Pluvicto), an FDA-approved radioactive treatment for advanced prostate cancer. The study tests whether spacing out doses differently can improve quality of life without reducing how long patients live. This is important because it could make an existing treatment more tolerable for patients.

items.title: AMO959 Combined With Lu-177 PSMA for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Phase 1b/2 trial evaluates AMO959 combined with Lu-177 PSMA (Pluvicto) and hormone therapy in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting patients who have tried one previous hormone treatment. It aims to determine safety and effectiveness of this combination approach.

items.title: Adding Docetaxel Chemotherapy to Hormone Therapy for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares adding docetaxel chemotherapy to standard hormone therapy plus apalutamide versus hormone therapy and apalutamide alone. The study is recruiting patients with newly metastatic prostate cancer to see if adding chemotherapy early improves outcomes. This could change how doctors approach initial treatment of advanced disease.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1/2 trial tests ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd), an antibody-drug conjugate, alone or combined with other treatments in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and measures PSA levels and safety. This represents a newer class of targeted therapies being explored for advanced prostate cancer.

items.title: Darolutamide Maintenance Treatment for Pretreated Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial studies darolutamide as maintenance therapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who have already received previous hormone treatments. The study is recruiting and builds on earlier research showing this approach can delay cancer progression. This addresses treatment challenges in heavily pretreated patients.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares mevrometostat (an investigational drug) combined with enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who haven't received prior hormone inhibitor treatments. The study is recruiting and represents a potentially important new treatment combination for advanced disease.

items.title: Sipuleucel-T Vaccine Combined With Bipolar Androgen Therapy for mCRPC
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial combines Sipuleucel-T (Provenge), an FDA-approved immunotherapy vaccine, with bipolar androgen therapy in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and measures immune response to the treatment combination. This explores whether hormone manipulation can enhance vaccine effectiveness.

items.title: AZD2265 Radioligand Therapy Versus Standard Treatment for mCRPC
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial compares AZD2265, a new PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy, to standard treatments in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and measures progression-free survival and overall survival. This is a major trial of a new radioactive treatment similar to Lu-177 PSMA.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 3 trial tests mevrometostat combined with enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone in patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer who haven't received prior hormone treatments or chemotherapy. The study is recruiting and could establish a new standard treatment for newly metastatic disease.

items.title: BPX-601 CAR T-Cell Therapy for Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 1 trial tests BPX-601, a CAR T-cell therapy made from the patient's own immune cells, in advanced treatment-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting to determine safety, best dose, and effectiveness. CAR T-cell therapy is a cutting-edge immunotherapy approach that has worked in blood cancers.

items.title: XL092 Treatment for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This Phase 2 trial evaluates XL092, an oral medication taken once daily, in patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and will assess how well the drug works after 16 weeks and monitor safety. This represents another targeted therapy option being explored.

items.title: Inflammation Pathways Drive Treatment Resistance in Advanced Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This research paper describes how chronic inflammation activates specific cellular pathways (NFκB and JAK/STAT3) that help prostate cancer survive and resist treatment. These inflammatory signals work together with hormone signaling to promote cancer growth, spread, and resistance to castration therapy. Understanding these mechanisms could lead to new treatments targeting inflammation in advanced disease.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Boosts Immune Response and Checkpoint Blockade
items.summary: This study developed a new DNA vaccine targeting PSMA, a protein highly expressed in aggressive prostate cancer. The vaccine improved immune response against tumors and enhanced the effectiveness of PD-1 checkpoint blockade immunotherapy. In animal models, the vaccine prevented cancer spread to lungs and increased immune system activation against tumors.

items.title: Metformin Reduces Kidney Radiation Dose During Lu-177 PSMA Therapy
items.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
items.summary: This study found that metformin, a common diabetes drug, reduces radiation dose to the kidneys during Lu-177 PSMA radioligand therapy without affecting tumor treatment. This is important because kidney damage is a concern with this therapy. The finding suggests metformin might protect kidneys while maintaining cancer treatment effectiveness.

items.title: Kidney Function After Lu-177 PSMA Therapy in mCRPC Patients
items.source: European journal of nuclear medicine and molecular imaging
items.summary: This study tracked kidney function over time in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients receiving Lu-177 PSMA therapy. Understanding long-term kidney effects is important for patient safety and treatment planning with this radioactive therapy. The research helps doctors monitor and manage potential kidney complications.

items.title: Imaging Metrics Predict Response to Lu-177 PSMA Treatment
items.summary: This study found that specific imaging measurements from Lu-177 PSMA scans can predict how well patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer respond to treatment. Being able to predict treatment response earlier could help doctors adjust therapy plans and avoid ineffective treatments. This could improve outcomes by personalizing treatment approaches.
